summary: Milestone 2026.05.240 recorded 0 experiments in the timing window per authoritative TIMING DATA; no compute-bound tasks were tracked. Both GPUs were idle (0% utilization, 5 MB allocated each) throughout the milestone window, consistent with the absence of any GGUF/CUDA workloads.
bottlenecks_identified: No experiment commits were captured in the TIMING DATA window for this milestone; the conductor's git-commit-based timing probe found no milestone-scoped experiment artifacts to measure.

GPU memory residuals (5 MB on each RTX 3090) with 0% utilization suggest idle processes that were not cleaned up between milestones, which can interfere with memory-headroom checks in subsequent compute-bound tasks.
improvements_suggested: Ensure the conductor's milestone-activation commit includes a sentinel marker so the git-log timing probe can anchor the milestone window correctly, preventing 0-experiment reports on milestones that did run experiments.
Add a post-milestone GPU memory flush step (torch.cuda.empty_cache() / explicit process teardown) so residual 5 MB allocations do not accumulate across milestones.
Pre-stage the next milestone roadmap (research-roadmap-next.yaml) before archiving the current one to avoid the blocked_roadmap_missing cascade pattern observed in .222-.227.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Fix the conductor's timing-probe anchor so all milestone experiments are captured in TIMING DATA, eliminating spurious 0-experiment retros that obscure real throughput.
Add automated GPU-memory-flush to the milestone teardown hook so neither RTX 3090 carries idle allocations into the next milestone's precondition checks.

Enforce pre-staged roadmap discipline (research-roadmap-next.yaml present before archive step) to prevent the blocked_roadmap_missing recurrence pattern that has idled multiple consecutive milestones.
meta_reflection: This milestone produced a 0-experiment retro because the timing probe found no commits in its window — not because no work was done. The primary operational lesson is that the measurement infrastructure itself is a bottleneck: a retro that cannot see its own milestone's experiments cannot surface real slowdowns. Fixing the probe anchor is higher-leverage than any experiment-level optimization.
